claims.quote: if, by good luck, there were a ring like Saturn’s which stretched round the world
claims.description: A ring around the earth above Greenwich would let any observer work out longitude from its apparent height.

claims.quote: if any one would build a good tall tower at Greenwich, straight into the sky
claims.description: A tower about a hundred miles high would serve as a fixed landmark for measuring longitude.

claims.quote: Suppose one over the meridian of Greenwich, and the other over that of New Orleans.
claims.description: Two artificial moons placed in orbit would give a navigator a reference body almost anywhere on the globe.

claims.quote: if you drove it so fast and far that when its power of ascent was exhausted, and it began to fall, it should clear the earth, and pass outside the North Pole
claims.description: A huge launcher would throw a large payload into a permanent orbit around the earth.

claims.quote: we would build two gigantic fly-wheels
claims.description: Two enormous flywheels would store energy from a waterfall and fling the moon into orbit.

claims.quote: The curve it is now on will forever clear the world
claims.description: The launched moon would follow an orbit that never returns it to the earth.

claims.quote: then we could measure the longitude from that
claims.description: Observers could fix their longitude by watching a high orbiting object rise above their horizon.

claims.quote: on the Brick Moon young Herschel will be able to see a dab of mortar a foot and a half long, if he wants to
claims.description: A telescope on the artificial moon could resolve details a foot and a half across from far away.

claims.quote: should begin its course of eternal blessings in one unchanging meridian
claims.description: The launched moon would serve seamen indefinitely as a fixed longitude reference.

claims.quote: With this power he made an ice lens, ten feet in diameter
claims.description: Commentary describes a ten-foot lens made of ice, the story's invention for a huge telescope.
